question: There are two circles with radii of 5 cm and 3 cm are positioned so that they touch each other internally. What is the distance between their centers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centers is the difference of their radii.

Distance (d) = R₁ − R₂

d = 5 − 3 = 2 cm

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the first circle (R) = 5 cm

Radius of the second circle (r) = 3 cm

**Formula Used:**

For two circles touching internally, distance between centers (d) = |R − r|

 Radius R = 5 cm (C1 to P)
 Radius r = 3 cm (C2 to P)
 d = 2 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the centers be C₁ and C₂ and the point of contact be P.

⇒ C₁P = Radius 1 = 5 cm

⇒ C₂P = Radius 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Since they touch internally, centers and the point of contact are collinear.

⇒ Distance C₁C₂ = C₁P − C₂P

⇒ Distance = 5 − 3

⇒ Distance = 2 cm

**∴ The correct option is (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Externally Touching Circles

When two circles touch each other externally, the distance between their centers is the sum of their radii: d = R₁ + R₂.

Intersecting Circles

If two circles intersect at two distinct points, the distance between their centers (d) satisfies the condition: |R₁ − R₂| R₁ + R₂.</p
